title: Smooth base change
statement:
Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X & \xleftarrow{\;h\;} & Y\\
f\downarrow & & \downarrow e\\
S & \xleftarrow{\;g\;} & T
\end{array}
$$

be Cartesian with $f$ smooth and $g$ quasi-compact
quasi-separated, and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. Then for
every $q$ and every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\Et}$
all of whose geometric stalks are torsion of orders invertible on $S$
(each element killed by a positive integer invertible on $S$),

$$
f^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F,
$$

the map being the base-change map of [sk-def-bc].

proof.text: Coefficient comparison used below. For any commutative coefficient ring $R$, apply [lem-sbc-base-change-restrict-scalars-arrow] to $\mathbf Z\to R$. Thus forgetting scalars identifies the whole degree-$q$ base-change arrow with the abelian-sheaf base-change arrow, not merely its source and target. Here $\mathbf Z$-module sheaves are abelian sheaves, and [sbc-def-base-change-map] identifies their adjunction-defined maps. Scalar restriction reflects isomorphisms: the inverse of a bijective $R$-linear map $a$ is $R$-linear, since $a(r a^{-1}(y))=r y=a(a^{-1}(r y))$. Consequently the abelian locality and composition statements used below apply to $R$-module arrows as well. No flatness of $\mathbf Z\to R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0D6J, lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded (3); Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; canonical comparison as stated in the cited node

proof.text: In degree $q<0$, compute the higher direct image of a sheaf by an injective resolution in degrees $\geq0$, as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The pushed-forward complex has zero terms below zero and hence zero cohomology there. Exactness of the constant-module inverse images [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies both sides of the map of [sbc-def-base-change-map] with zero. For $q=0$, [sbc-lem-degree-zero-flat-base-change] applies directly: its last sentence includes every smooth $f$ and every sheaf of sets, with no restriction on $g$. The degree-zero map is its adjunction-unit map by [sbc-def-base-change-map]. Inverse image on modules has the underlying inverse image and unit/counit on abelian sheaves by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; the same maps of underlying sets therefore show that this module map is invertible (its set inverse respects addition and scalar multiplication by injectivity). These cases require no torsion hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change, second proof, first paragraph; Tag 0EYS, lemma-fppf-reduced-fibres-base-change-f-star

proof.text: Fix $q\geq0$. Write $\mathcal F=\varinjlim_n\mathcal F[n]$ using [sk-def-smooth], indexed by positive integers invertible on $S$, ordered by divisibility. This is a small nonempty filtered poset: $1$ belongs to it and $nm$ is an upper bound of $n,m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], $h$ is qcqs since it is the base change of $g$. The two higher-image functors preserve this filtered colimit by [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-large-filtered-colimit], and $f^{-1},e^{-1}$ preserve it because they are left adjoints by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Naturality of the base-change map [sk-def-bc] makes its value at $\mathcal F$ the colimit of the maps at $\mathcal F[n]$. If these maps are invertible their inverses commute with the transition maps, so the induced map on the two colimits has the colimit of these inverses as its inverse. By [lem-sbc-quotient-coefficients-base-change], it is therefore enough to prove $\mathrm{BC}(f,R,q)$ for every commutative ring $R$ with $nR=0$ for some positive $n$ invertible on $S$: take $R=\Lambda/n\Lambda$ for the sheaf $\mathcal F[n]$. The quotient-ring lemma identifies the actual module-valued arrow.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change, second proof, filtered torsion paragraph; coefficient step in Coefficients.lean

proof.text: For these fixed coefficients, [sbc-lem-etale-locality], applied to the underlying abelian arrow using step 1, allows simultaneous etale localization on $X$ and $S$ exactly as in its displayed diagrams. All new direct-image morphisms are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. This also proves the etale case in every degree without using the theorem being proved: if $f:X\to S$ is etale, take the covering $U=X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}X$, the etale base neighbourhood $V=X\xrightarrow{f}S$, and $U\to V=\mathrm{id}_X$. The localized square is the identity square with direct-image map $h:Y\to X$ and coefficient sheaf $e^{-1}\mathcal F$. Its exchange map is the identity, since the unit and counit for the identity functor are identities in the formula of [sbc-def-base-change-map]. Locality gives the result for $f$. This includes relative dimension zero.

source.place: Tag 0EZR, lemma-base-change-local, clauses (1) and (3); identity case of Tag 07A7

proof.text: Let $a:U\to V$ be a fixed affine smooth morphism of relative dimension one with $U$ affine, and let $nR=0$ with $n>0$ invertible on $V$. Prove by strong induction on $q\geq0$ that $\mathrm{BC}(a,R,q)$ holds universally in the exact sense of [sk-def-bc]. Its degree-zero case holds after every base change by step 2, since the base-changed morphism remains smooth of relative dimension one by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]; the negative-degree cases also hold universally by step 2. At $q\geq1$, the induction hypotheses give the universal property in every nonnegative degree less than $q$, and negative degrees have just been dealt with. Thus all hypotheses of [sk-lem-induction] are satisfied and it gives the universal degree-$q$ property. This is induction for the fixed $a$; it never asserts that its source stays affine after an arbitrary base change. Specializing the universal assertion to the identity of $V$ proves $\mathrm{BC}(a,R,q)$ in all degrees.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, second proof, reduction to affine smooth relative dimension one; induction packaged by the current blueprint sk-lem-induction

proof.text: For a general smooth $f$ and fixed $nR=0$, apply step 4 and [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] to cover by charts with $X,S$ affine and $f$ equal to an etale map $X\to\mathbf A^d_S$ followed by its projection. On such a chart factor the projection as $\mathbf A^d_S\to\mathbf A^{d-1}_S\to\cdots\to\mathbf A^1_S\to S$. By the polynomial-ring description in [def-sbc-affine-space], each map is an affine-line projection over an affine scheme; it is affine, has affine source, and is smooth of relative dimension one by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. Step 5 applies to each projection, since the image of the unit $n$ is a unit on every intermediate base. Step 4 applies to the initial etale map. Apply [sbc-lem-base-change-composition] repeatedly to the underlying abelian squares and then use step 1 to reflect the resulting isomorphism in the module category. The intermediate direct-image maps are base changes of the qcqs $g$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], so every application is valid. For $d=0$ the projection $\mathbf A^0_S\to S$ is the identity under [def-sbc-affine-space], and step 4 handles the chart directly. Finally step 4 descends these isomorphisms from the covering charts. Hence $\mathrm{BC}(f,R,q)$ holds for every smooth $f$ and every $q$ for these coefficients.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, second proof, etale-local affine-space paragraph; Tag 054L, morphisms-lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space; Tag 0EZS, lemma-base-change-compose

proof.text: Apply step 6 with $R=\Lambda/n\Lambda$ for each positive $n$ invertible on $S$. The quotient-coefficient lemma [lem-sbc-quotient-coefficients-base-change] proves that the original degree-$q$ module map at $\mathcal F[n]$ is an isomorphism. The colimit argument of step 3 now gives the claimed map at $\mathcal F$ for $q\geq0$; step 2 already proves it for $q<0$. Throughout, the arrow is the canonical map of [sk-def-bc], not an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism between its two objects.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, second proof, conclusion of filtered-torsion reduction

blueprint_update.statement:
Consider a cartesian square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X' & \xrightarrow{\ u\ } & X\\
{\scriptstyle f'}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle f}\\
Y' & \xrightarrow{\ g\ } & Y
\end{array}
$$

and the exchange map $\operatorname{Ex}_{g,f}:g^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*u^*$ of
[sk-lem-sbc-exchange-compatibility].
Suppose $g$ is smooth and $f$ is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $F$ be a classical torsion
abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ which is the filtered union of its
subsheaves $F[n]$ for the positive integers $n$ invertible on $Y$.
Then for every $q\geq0$ the degree-$q$ exchange map induced by
$\operatorname{Ex}_{g,f}$, a morphism of abelian sheaves on $Y'_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$,

$$
 g^*R^qf_*F\longrightarrow R^qf'_*u^*F
$$

is an isomorphism.

*Complement.* In the notation of [sk-def-bc], where the smooth morphism is called $f$ and the
qcqs one $g$, let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X & \xleftarrow{\;h\;} & Y\\
f\downarrow & & \downarrow e\\
S & \xleftarrow{\;g\;} & T
\end{array}
$$

be Cartesian with $f$ smooth and $g$ quasi-compact
quasi-separated, and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. Then for
every $q$ and every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\Et}$
all of whose geometric stalks are torsion of orders invertible on $S$
(each element killed by a positive integer invertible on $S$),

$$
f^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F,
$$

the map being the base-change map of [sk-def-bc].

proof.text:
Since $F$ is classical, $F=\nu_X^*F_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ for a torsion abelian sheaf
$F_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ on $X_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$. Since $f$ and $f'$ are qcqs,
[sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] and
[sk-lem-sbc-exchange-compatibility] identify both sides and the
exchange map with the inverse images of their étale models. The proof
below therefore takes place on the étale sites, and in it $g^{-1}$
denotes inverse image of étale sheaves.

Fix an integer $n$ invertible on $Y$. For $r\geq0$, $\mathrm{BC}(g,n,r)$ means: for every
scheme $T$ over $Y$, Noetherian or not and not necessarily of finite type over $k$, every
qcqs morphism $Z\to T$, every sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules $M$ on $Z_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$,
and every $0\leq i\leq r$, the degree-$i$ exchange map for the square with base change
$Y'\times_YT\to T$ and direct image along $Z\to T$ is an isomorphism
([Stacks, Tag 0F02](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F02)).

The exchange map is local for étale coverings of $Y'$ and of $Y$,
since restriction to an étale object is localization of the site, and
exchange maps compose when two base changes are composed
([Stacks, Tag 0EZR](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZR),
[Stacks, Tag 0EZS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZS)). Both facts hold in each
fixed degree and for the property $\mathrm{BC}(g,n,r)$.
For smooth $g$, étale coordinates
([Stacks, Tag 054L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/054L)) give, locally on
$Y'$ and $Y$ and with all schemes affine, a factorization

$$
 Y'\longrightarrow\mathbf A^{d-1}_Y
   \longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\mathbf A^1_Y
   \longrightarrow Y,
$$

whose first arrow is an étale map to $\mathbf A^d_Y$ followed by
projection; each displayed arrow is smooth of relative dimension one.
The case $d=0$ is étale localization. It therefore suffices, in the
induction on the degree, to treat affine $Y$ and $Y'$ with $g$ smooth of
relative dimension one.
Finally, $F$ is the filtered union of the subsheaves $F[n]$, ordered by divisibility of
integers invertible on $Y$. Inverse image commutes with this colimit,
and so do higher direct images along qcqs morphisms
([Stacks, Tag 09Z1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z1)).
It therefore suffices to treat $\mathbf Z/n$-modules for each such $n$.

A smooth morphism is flat, locally of finite presentation, and has
geometrically reduced fibres, so degree zero is
[sk-prop-deg0]. Let $q\geq1$ and assume the theorem in
all degrees less than $q$. Fix $n$ invertible on $Y$. Smoothness is
stable under base change, so the induction hypothesis applied after
every base change $T\to Y$ gives $\mathrm{BC}(g,n,q-1)$. By étale
coordinates and composition of exchange maps it suffices to treat $g$
affine and smooth of relative dimension one.

If $\mathrm{BC}(g,n,q)$ failed, [sk-lem-universal-datum]
would give $S$, $C$, $h$ and $d$ with $R^qh_*\underline{\mathbf Z/d}\neq0$,
contradicting [sk-thm-vanishing]. Hence
$\mathrm{BC}(g,n,q)$ holds, and so degree $q$ holds for every smooth $g$
and every sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules. The filtered union of the
$F[n]$ gives the theorem for $F$, and
[sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] transports the isomorphism and
the exchange map from the étale sites to $Y'_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$.

*Complement.* *Negative degrees*: both sides vanish for $q<0$.
*Degree zero*: [sk-prop-deg0] (smooth is flat, of finite
presentation, with geometrically reduced fibres).
*Filtered torsion*: $\mathcal F=\varinjlim_n\mathcal F[n]$
over the integers $n$ invertible on $S$, where $\mathcal F[n]$ is the
$n$-torsion subsheaf; inverse images are left adjoints and
$R^qg_*$, $R^qh_*$ commute with filtered colimits for qcqs $g,h$;
so it suffices to handle sheaves annihilated by a single $n$
invertible on $S$. Such a sheaf is a sheaf of $\Lambda/n\Lambda$-modules, and
the higher direct images and the base-change map of a sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules are those of its underlying abelian sheaf, hence also those
computed for $\Lambda/n\Lambda$-modules. So it suffices to prove
$\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q)$ for every $q\ge0$ and every coefficient ring
$\Lambda$ in which some $n$ invertible on $S$ vanishes.
*Reduction to relative dimension one*: the assertion is
étale local on $X$ and $S$; the relative dimension of $f$ is locally
constant, so we may assume it constant, equal to $d$; by [sk-prop-normal-form] one may
assume $X$ and $S$
affine and $X\to S$ factoring as an étale morphism to $\Aaf^d_S$ followed by
the projection; writing $\Aaf^d_S\to \Aaf^{d-1}_S\to\cdots\to\Aaf^1_S\to S$
and using the composition compatibility of the base-change map (and that
étale morphisms satisfy base change trivially), it suffices to prove
the assertion for affine smooth $X\to S$ of relative dimension one
with $X$ affine; $n$ remains invertible on each intermediate base.
*Induction on $q$*: for such $f$, prove by strong induction on $q$ that
$\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q)$ holds universally. For $q\le0$ this is the
negative-degree and degree-zero cases applied to every base change of $f$
(again smooth). For $q\ge1$, with the statement known universally in all
degrees $<q$, [sk-lem-induction] gives $\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q)$
universally. Specialising along the identity of $S$ gives
$\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q)$, and running the filtered colimit back over $n$
finishes the proof.
